validityChecks.title: Default zero slippage on BalancerPooler enables sandwich attacks on every mint via 3-parameter mint() overload

checks.evidence: A 4-parameter mint overload exists at NFTMinter.sol:121 that accepts extraData for slippage protection. User choosing the 3-param overload could be considered a user mistake.
checks.counterArgument: The 3-parameter function provides no mechanism for the caller to specify slippage even if they wanted to. This is a structural gap in the interface, not a user forgetting a parameter.

checks.evidence: Zero slippage defaults are a well-known DeFi anti-pattern commonly flagged by automated tools.
checks.counterArgument: The finding goes beyond the common pattern by identifying the structural impossibility of setting slippage through the 3-param overload. The 4-param overload's existence makes the gap non-obvious.

severityAssessment.reasoning: Strongest argument for Medium: the 3-param mint interface makes it structurally impossible for callers to specify slippage, unlike typical 'default to zero' patterns where the parameter exists but is optional. Strongest argument for QA: the 4-param overload provides the safe path, and zero-slippage convenience functions are an accepted DeFi pattern.
severityAssessment.riskOfDowngrade: HIGH - judges frequently downgrade zero-slippage defaults to QA

validityChecks.notes: Flagged for human review. The finding's validity hinges on whether the 3-param overload's inability to pass slippage is a 'protocol design gap' (Medium) or 'user should use the right function' (QA).

validityChecks.title: Unchecked 1:1 phUSD minting with UNBALANCED addLiquidity causes suboptimal BPT returns when pool ratio diverges

checks.evidence: The _normalizeToPhUSD function name suggests deliberate 1:1 design. The function is purely mechanical decimal scaling.
checks.counterArgument: Intentional 1:1 normalization combined with UNBALANCED addLiquidity produces quantified value loss (26-46% at realistic ratios). No compensating mechanism exists. The NatSpec documents what the function does, not that the economic consequences were considered.

severityAssessment.reasoning: Systematic protocol-level value leak on every mint when pool ratios diverge. BPT loss is quantified and significant. Protocol bears the loss directly. No attacker action required beyond normal arbitrage. Matches C4 Medium: 'value leak with stated assumptions.'

validityChecks.notes: No invalid patterns detected. Strong finding with concrete economic analysis.

validityChecks.notes: Defense-in-depth recommendation. Correctly identified as not currently exploitable. Appropriately Low.

validityChecks.title: BalancerPooler.unlockCallback lacks explicit reentrancy protection

validityChecks.title: Dispatcher contracts lack token recovery mechanism
validityChecks.notes: Missing rescue function for stuck tokens (dust from rounding, accidental sends). Not a user mistake pattern since rounding dust accumulation is protocol-caused.

validityChecks.title: NFTMinter hardcodes ATokenDispatcher cast for all dispatchers
validityChecks.notes: Design coupling concern. Concrete type cast prevents alternative dispatcher implementations. Appropriately Low.

validityChecks.title: All claim NFTs minted with same token ID regardless of payment context
validityChecks.notes: Design observation about undifferentiated claim tokens. Appropriately Low -- no direct vulnerability claimed.

validityChecks.title: Owner can set price to zero, permanently breaking multiplicative growth formula

checks.evidence: Requires owner to call setPrice(0) -- a direct admin action. Owner should know not to set price to zero.
checks.counterArgument: The finding is about missing input validation, not admin trust. The multiplicative formula being permanently broken by zero is a subtle consequence that may not be obvious to an admin.

validityChecks.notes: Borderline admin-mistake pattern. Defensible as 'missing input validation' but could be challenged. Keep as Low but expect possible pushback.

validityChecks.title: Missing SafeERC20 causes permanent revert for USDT and non-bool-returning tokens

checks.evidence: Finding specifically mentions USDT. USDT is the ONE exception to the non-standard token rule per C4.
checks.exception: USDT exception applies -- VALID per C4 Supreme Court ruling

validityChecks.notes: VALID because the USDT exception applies. USDT's non-standard transfer return value is a known, accepted concern that C4 considers valid. Without the USDT angle, this would be INVALID as a non-standard token finding.

validityChecks.title: Price growth calculated on gross price instead of actualReceived for FOT tokens

checks.evidence: Finding is specifically about fee-on-transfer token behavior.
checks.counterArgument: The codebase explicitly supports FOT tokens: balance-before/after pattern in NFTMinter._executeMint (lines 141-143), balance-before/after in BalancerPooler.unlockCallback (lines 78-80), NatSpec says 'FOT-adjusted amount' (line 63), MockFOTToken.sol test mock exists. FOT support is clearly intended.

validityChecks.notes: FLAG because FOT findings are normally invalid, but strong evidence exists that FOT is intentionally in scope for this project (MockFOTToken, balance-before/after patterns, FOT-specific NatSpec). The finding identifies incomplete FOT handling in a codebase that otherwise supports FOT. Recommend keeping as VALID Low.

validityChecks.title: Uncapped growthBasisPoints allows owner to effectively halt minting via price escalation

checks.evidence: Requires owner to set extreme growthBasisPoints value.
checks.counterArgument: Centralization Risk is a specific C4 category designed for documenting owner capabilities. The finding documents the capability and its impact without claiming malicious intent. This is the exact purpose of C-labeled findings.

validityChecks.notes: FLAG because admin-mistake pattern is partially detected. However, C4 Centralization Risk is the designated category for this type of finding. Valid as C-01 but would be INVALID if submitted as Medium/High.
